names.name: Paczki Day
names.said: Bakeries post a limit per customer and mean it.

text.what: The Tuesday before Lent, kept in Polish-American cities — Chicago, Milwaukee, Detroit, Windsor — as a day for eating pączki.
text.story:
Pączki are traditionally eaten in Poland on the Thursday before Lent. In Polish communities in the United States the observance moved to Fasnacht Day — the Tuesday — which puts Polish and Pennsylvania Dutch traditions on the same morning.

Hamtramck, Michigan, a city surrounded by Detroit with deep Polish roots, is the best-known American centre of the day.
text.today: Lines start before dawn; bakeries fry all night ahead of it and sell until the dough runs out.

kin.as: The other tradition on the same Tuesday.

geo.note: the town the day is most associated with, not a venue
